name: Kanda
tagline: Tokyo in 3 minutes and Otemachi in 9 minutes. Served by 4 lines.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, served by JR Yamanote Line, JR Chuo Rapid Line, JR Keihin-Tohoku Line and Tokyo Metro Ginza Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 9 minutes to Otemachi, 13 minutes to Shinjuku, 22 minutes to Shibuya and 17 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 4.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.1 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 4.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.8 m to 5.9 m, a difference of 2.1 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 6 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 30 clinics and 29 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 同仁記念会明和病院, about 386 m away and 秋葉原メディカルクリニック, about 626 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 4 lines serve the station: JR Yamanote Line, JR Chuo Rapid Line, JR Keihin-Tohoku Line and Tokyo Metro Ginza Line. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 3 lines and Tokyo Metro runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 85.

neighbours.note: 501 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Kanda.
591 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 7 minutes sooner than Kanda.
